title: Renewal conversation map — Avalon Insurance (QBR prep)
content:
Purpose and framing: This is a working conversation map and slide-by-slide script for the upcoming QBR with Avalon Insurance (strategic account, renewal window Q2 2025). Primary goals: 1) surface clear ROI/cost-per-token trends; 2) align on product roadmap items that unblock Avalon's compliance and throughput goals; 3) surface a tailored renewal proposal with optional Dedicated capacity + 12-month commit; 4) identify immediate wins we can deliver in 30/90/180 day bands to reduce churn risk.

Meeting logistics (prep):
- Attendees (Redwood): Priya Nair (CS lead), Daniel Kim (Solutions Eng), Marcus Lee (Customer Reliability), Sales AE: Alejandra Torres (on optional renewal negotiation).
- Avalon attendees expected: Head of AI Ops, VP Product (decision maker), Infra Lead (technical), Procurement (budget).
- Duration: 60 minutes. Recommend structure: 10m exec recap / business metrics, 20m usage & technical health, 15m roadmap & ask, 10m renewal options + commercial, 5m next steps.

High-level talking points (for Execs):
- Thank you for the partnership; show appreciation for integration work on the underwriting pipeline.
- The ask: we want to make renewal an easy decision by ensuring predictability and delivering two concrete latency/cost wins before contract signature.
- Risk/mitigant (proactively): highlight scaled usage spikes during end-of-quarter underwriting runs; propose burst pool and pre-warming as a mitigation.

Account health snapshot (scripted bullets to read while showing metric slides):
- Monthly active inference jobs: 1.2M (up 82% YoY).
- Average 99th percentile latency: 320ms (target 250ms) — spike correlated with long-sequence batch jobs in underwriting flows.
- Cost per 1k tokens (hosted): $4.80 (down from $5.70 after caching tweaks in Oct) — show trend chart.
- Error rate (5xx): 0.9% last 90 days, concentrated in one geographic region during patch windows.
- Adoption highlights: internal tooling teams adopted embeddings for search prototype (pilot stage).

Slide-by-slide narrative (speaker notes + cues):
- Slide 1: Welcome & Goals (Priya)
  - Note: Keep slide visual minimal. Read: "Today we want to confirm three things: performance baseline, risk mitigations, and an agreement for capacity and price that supports Avalon’s growth. We'll leave time for procurement questions at the end."

- Slide 2: Business context & usage story (Priya)
  - Show: Top-level usage table (jobs, tokens, peak concurrency). Script: "In Q4 you scaled more than expected; this is good but it exposed two operational friction points we can remove together."

- Slide 3: Health dashboard (Marcus)
  - Show: latency percentiles, error trend line, region map. Script: "99p latency is above your SLA in underwriting windows; we hypothesize batch queueing and cold KV caches are the root cause. We propose targeted cache warming + prioritized bursting to bring 99p under 250ms."

- Slide 4: Root cause evidence & mitigation plan (Marcus + Daniel)
  - Show: tracer sample, batch distribution heatmap. Script: "Observed request size distribution and server traces show long-tail due to a single job category. Options: per-route batching config + model variant routing to smaller context models for back-office jobs."

- Slide 5: Product roadmap alignment & asks (Daniel)
  - Show: near-term feature list (KV cache pinning, per-route priority queuing, quantization test for selected model). Script: "We can prioritize two engineering items as part of a joint success plan: (1) per-route KV pinning to reduce cold start, and (2) trial of 8-bit quantized variant for underwriting heuristics to reduce cost by ~20%."

- Slide 6: Renewal options (Priya + Alejandra)
  - Present three options:
    A) 12-mo Dedicated baseline (recommended): reserved pool sized to expected peak, 10% discount vs hosted over usage baseline, 99.9% uptime SLA.
    B) 12-mo Hosted + burst credits: lower commitment, higher overage, includes two weeks of priority engineering for rollout.
    C) Pilot Dedicated (90-day): transition period to validate SLOs before full commit.
  - Script: "We’ve modeled the options against your Q3 forecast; option A gives the most predictable unit economics as you scale."

- Slide 7: Commercial levers & negotiation points (Alejandra)
  - Script: "We can flex on the commit level (50k vs 100k token commitments), include one free migration sprint, and lock in 12-month pricing for embedded model variants if you commit by end of Q2."

- Slide 8: Case study insert (brief)
  - Use anonymized insurance peer example: "Peer reduced 99p latency by 35% after per-route batching + dedicated pool. This removed manual failover work and improved SLAs for their customer-facing flows."

- Slide 9: Risks & escalation path (Priya)
  - Script: "If we see repeat latency breaches after mitigation, we'll kick off SRE-runbook + on-call rotation for 30 days and propose a short-term dedicated burst pool until root cause is fixed."

- Slide 10: Action plan (30/90/180 day milestones)
  - 0–30 days: agree on option A or B, schedule migration sprint, perform initial KV pinning and cache warm tests.
  - 30–90 days: deploy per-route batching, run quantization pilot, measure cost/latency.
  - 90–180 days: ramp Dedicated pool, finalize runbook, quarterly check-in cadence.

Tailored conversation prompts (questions to surface during the meeting):
- "Which internal SLAs do you prioritize during end-of-quarter runs — latency or throughput?"
- "What would a successful Dedicated rollout look like to your procurement team?"
- "Are there downstream stakeholders (legal/compliance) who need a technical summary of the private deployment option?"

Negotiation playbook notes (internal tips):
- Prioritize getting a technical commitment (ok to start migration work) before settling final price. If procurement pushes back, propose Pilot Dedicated with a conversion clause.
- Use migration sprint as demonstration of value: deliver KV pinning + one 99p latency report within sprint.
- If Avalon requests lower unit cost, trade for a longer commit or an expanded support tier instead of deeper discount.

Open items we must finalize before the meeting: (use as checklist)
- Confirm Avalon attendee list and whether Procurement will join.
- Validate Q3 forecast numbers (pull from finance) to model commit levels.
- Prepare custom cost model slide (Daniel) with per-option projections.
- Prepare a short technical appendix on data residency & KMS options for Private deployment.

Post-meeting commitments (template wording for email follow-up):
- "Thanks for your time today — here’s a summary of what we agreed and the immediate next steps. We will: 1) schedule migration sprint kickoff; 2) run KV pinning validation; 3) deliver a revised commercial proposal within 5 business days."

Notes / scratchpad (things to remember while presenting):
- Keep the commercial section concise; shift to technical detail only if the Infra Lead asks.
- Avoid promising timelines longer than 30 days for mitigation; instead promise measurable milestones.
- Be prepared to show a demo of the observability dashboard and a short trace example.

Attachments to assemble (before saving final copy):
- Custom cost model sheet (linked_artifacts JIRA ticket).
- 2–3 exported trace samples for Marcus.
- One-pager on Dedicated vs Hosted feature differences (procurement facing).

Revision history (working doc):
- 2025-01-08: initial draft (Priya).
- 2025-01-20: added technical root-cause evidence (Marcus).
- 2025-02-03: inserted commercial levers and negotiation tips (Alejandra).

TODOs (assignments):
- Daniel: finalize cost projections and slide visuals (due 2025-02-07).
- Marcus: pull 3 representative traces and annotate (due 2025-02-05).
- Alejandra: draft renewal term sheet and concession matrix (due 2025-02-04).

This is intentionally a working script — please annotate inline with any missing numbers or pushbacks you expect from Avalon. The goal is to leave the meeting with a technical kickoff and a signed Letter of Intent or Pilot acceptance within 14 days.
